newsitem.title: POLAND: FORECAST RAINS THREATENS NEW POLISH FLOODS.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST RAINS THREATENS NEW POLISH FLOODS.

text.p: People in Poland and the Czech Republic, where floods have caused about 100 deaths and devastated huge swathes of countryside, were warned on Thursday that more destruction could be on the way.
Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz told Poland's parliament that weather forecasts predicted heavy rain overnight and into the weekend.

"Unfortunately we must expect the possibility of the start of another wave of floods," he told an emergency session of the lower house which passed 21 laws to deal with the region's worst natural disaster in decades.
Police put the death toll in Poland from the floods at 46, while police in the Czech Republic to the south said 46 people were killed there and three were missing.
The Czech Weather Service said more heavy rains were forecast in the flooded east Bohemia and Moravia regions, where up to 50 cm (19.5 inches) have fallen in the past two weeks.
The flood waters have destroyed or badly damaged hundreds of homes, cut road, rail and telecommunications links and swamped thousands of hectares of croplands.
Some economists estimated that the damage to the Czech economy could total up to 100 billion crowns ($2.9 billion).

Poland has called a day of mourning for Friday. New floods would strike people already ruined or exhausted by their ordeal, including the 650,000 residents of Wroclaw, thousands of whom laboured day and night on barricades to save their historic city's centre.

Cimoszewicz said he was sending extra troops to endangered areas to help to strengthen flood defences and urged residents, without panic, to prepare. "We must hope it will not happen, but let's be better prepared," he said.
Polish police estimated that 40,000 farms, 86 towns and 875 villages were hit and 4,500 sq km (1,700 square miles) of land was swamped.
Some flood waters receded in southern Poland, leaving a stench and risk of disease in shattered streets veiled in sewage, rubbish and dead animals.
But a wave of high water was advancing north along the Odra river and the German border, attacking new towns and villages.
On the German side of the border river, villagers in Ratzdorf furiously filled sandbanks as muddy brown water streamed into low-lying farmland and flooded into basements of houses.
Cimoszewicz phoned Hungary's Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Poland appealed to Germany and Sweden for urgent help, PAP news agency reported. Poland's main needs include heavy-duty pumps.

The Hungarian government pledged 350 million forints ($1.8 million) in flood disaster relief for Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia and said it was sending 15 high capacity pumps to Poland. REUTER
